a.d: Used when something possesses enough value to recommend, or is acceptable and tolerable.
ex: 이 소설은 스토리가 탄탄해서 시간 날 때 꼭 한번 **읽을 만해요**. — This novel has a solid story, so it is really worth reading when you have time.

b.d: Used when an action is strictly mandatory or required by rules and duties.
ex: 도서관 책은 대출 기한 내에 반드시 **반납해야 해요**. — Library books must be returned within the loan period.

im-c54-01.tip: Use -(으)ㄹ 만하다 for positive recommendations of value; use -아/어야 하다 for rules and obligations.

im-c54-02.h: -도록 하다 (Gentle Directive / Institutional Notice) vs -(으)세요 (Everyday Polite Request)

a.d: Used in official workplace or classroom contexts to deliver polite instructions backed by rules and guidelines.
ex: 보고서는 금요일 오후까지 반드시 **제출하도록 하세요**. — Please make sure to submit the report by Friday afternoon.

b.d: Standard polite request used in interpersonal situations without institutional procedural weight.
ex: 여기 서명하고 잠시만 **기다리세요**. — Please sign here and wait for a moment.

im-c54-02.tip: Use -도록 하세요 for formal announcements and workplace procedures; use -(으)세요 for simple polite requests.

im-c54-02.q: Fix the overly blunt sentence that sounds too casual for an official workplace guideline.

answers: 퇴근 전에는 반드시 사무실 전원을 끄도록 하세요.

퇴근 전에는 반드시 사무실 전원을 끄도록 합시다.
퇴근 전에는 반드시 사무실 전원을 끄도록 합시다
im-c54-02.hint: For official company-wide instructions, use -끄도록 하세요 or -끄도록 합시다.
im-c54-02.why: Workplace procedures and guidelines require the polite institutional form -도록 하세요.

im-c54-03.h: -지 그래요? (Present Gentle Suggestion) vs -지 그랬어요 (Empathetic Past Regret)

a.d: Used to suggest an alternative action kindly without imposing ('Why don't you...?').
ex: 머리가 아프면 약을 먹고 좀 **쉬지 그래요**? — If your head hurts, why don't you take some medicine and rest a bit?

b.d: Used when looking back at a past outcome with warmth or mild reproof ('You should have...').
ex: 그렇게 힘들었으면 진작 병원에 **가지 그랬어요**. — If it was that painful, you should have gone to the hospital earlier.

im-c54-03.tip: Use -지 그래요? for considerate present choices; use -지 그랬어요 for sympathetic reflection on past decisions.

im-c54-03.q: Fix the tense mismatch where present suggestion -지 그래 is erroneously used about yesterday's oversleeping.

im-c54-03.hint: When expressing sympathetic regret about a past occurrence, use the past form -자지 그랬어.
im-c54-03.why: Past events with disappointing outcomes call for the past-oriented regret form -지 그랬어.

im-c54-04.h: -(으)ㄹ 만하다 (Evaluating Quality & Value) vs -지 그래요? (Inviting Action Gently)

a.d: Focuses on the quality, usefulness, or merit of an experience or item ('It's worth doing').
ex: 이 전시회는 기획이 참신해서 한번 **가 볼 만해요**. — This exhibition is worth visiting because its curation is novel.

b.d: Focuses on nudging the listener to carry out a helpful action with ease and kindness ('Why not do it?').
ex: 주말에 심심하면 그 전시회에 한번 **다녀오지 그래요**? — If you're bored on the weekend, why don't you visit that exhibition?

im-c54-04.tip: Use -(으)ㄹ 만하다 to highlight value; use -지 그래요? to encourage action softly.

im-c54-04.q: Fix the awkward sentence that uses past regret form -지 그랬어요 when giving real-time polite advice to an ailing colleague.
im-c54-04.wrong: 지금 몸이 아프면 일찍 퇴근하지 그랬어요.
answers: 지금 몸이 아프면 일찍 퇴근하지 그래요?
지금 몸이 아프면 일찍 퇴근하지 그래요

지금 몸이 아프면 일찍 퇴근해 보지 그래요
im-c54-04.hint: When advising someone gently on what to do right now, use the present form -퇴근하지 그래요?.
im-c54-04.why: -지 그랬어요 expresses regret about the past; present guidance calls for -지 그래요?.
